clue.text: French player's agent

parts.note: a player on stage is an actor

explanation.surface: A French footballer or performer has a representative handling his deals.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a commercial agent who buys and sells on behalf of others.

clue.text: One might shoot red dwarf!

parts.note: a red dwarf is a kind of star in astronomy; read 'shoot' as film with a camera and the star becomes a celebrity of the screen

explanation.surface: Someone with a gun or a camera takes aim at a small dim star.
explanation.walkthrough: Red dwarf is a type of star, and a star of the cinema is what a camera crew shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen celebrity is filmed, i.e. shot, and is called a star, as a red dwarf is.

clue.text: The argument against was useful, and retained

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
something that served a purpose was useful

explanation.surface: A debater notes that the opposing case proved helpful and was kept on.
explanation.definitionFit: Conserved means kept or preserved, a synonym of retained.

clue.text: One has a row with vocal cockney equestrian

indicators.note: vocal says the word is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a cockney drops the H, so a horseman becomes 'orseman

explanation.surface: Someone argues with a loud London rider.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys (working-class Londoners) traditionally drop the initial H, so horseman is said 'orseman. 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower in a boat is someone who has a row, i.e. rows.

clue.text: "Farm fed" was misrepresented about unit stated

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
words that were misrepresented have been distorted, so the letters of Farm fed are rearranged

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, is a unit

explanation.surface: A quote about a farm's livestock was misreported regarding the stated unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was misrepresented' rearranges FARM FED to AFFRMED, and 'about' wraps it round I (unit).
explanation.definitionFit: Affirmed means declared or asserted, a synonym of stated.

clue.text: A good job it delivers on time!

definitions.text: A good job it delivers on time!

parts.words: A good job it delivers on time!
parts.note: read 'good job' as relief at a punctual service; the thing delivered is the mail, at the faster, pricier rate in Britain

explanation.surface: Relief that something arrives punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK, first class is the dearer Royal Mail service aimed at next-day delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: The premium letter service is meant to deliver promptly, a good thing when it does.

clue.text: Not feeling at home with hot fashionable chap

parts.note: in means at home
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
U stands for upper-class, socially acceptable or smart
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Someone cold-hearted lounges at home with a stylish, attractive man.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class, acceptable usage, here standing for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhuman means cruel and lacking compassion, i.e. without feeling.

clue.text: Growth one finds in labyrinth

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for the puzzle of passages

parts.note: a labyrinth is a maze
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something growing is discovered inside a labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is a crop, something that grows, i.e. growth in the sense of produce.

clue.text: Pokes around it to get the figures

indicators.note: around means the word for pokes surrounds the next piece

parts.note: digs are pokes, as in digs in the ribs

explanation.surface: Someone prods at something to get the numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits are numerals, i.e. figures 0 to 9.

clue.text: Fighters with feet of clay

parts.note: the idiom feet of clay means a hidden weakness, but taken literally it describes soldier statues modelled in fired earth

explanation.surface: Warriors with a secret weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feet of clay' is an idiom for a flaw; here it is literal: the life-size clay soldiers buried with China's first emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese army of clay soldiers literally has feet (and bodies) of fired clay.

clue.text: Both sides welcome individual sort of person

indicators.note: welcome means take in, so the outer letters hold the next piece

parts.note: L and R are left and right, both sides
one is an individual

explanation.surface: Each side greets a solitary type.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner is a particular kind of person, one who prefers solitude.

clue.text: One of us has to lean right, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of lean right could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: One of us must tilt to the right politically, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges LEAN RIGHT; 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthling is an inhabitant of Earth, a human like us.

clue.text: Cooking vessel

parts.note: a pan for cooking with steam, and also a ship, a vessel powered by steam

explanation.walkthrough: Both readings fit: a pan that cooks by steam, and a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is both a pot for steaming food and a steam-powered ship.

clue.text: Office worker set off in a storm

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

indicators.note: off means the letters of set are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A temporary secretary storms off in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET to EST; 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm.

clue.text: Windows operating system that's festive

parts.note: sounds like computer software, but means a seasonal system of little windows opened one a day before Christmas

explanation.surface: A Christmas edition of Microsoft's software.
explanation.walkthrough: Windows is the Microsoft operating system, but here it means the little doors opened daily through December.
explanation.definitionFit: This countdown card has numbered windows opened day by day before Christmas.

clue.text: Uncooked tuna — a rule that's variable

indicators.note: variable means changeable, so the letters of tuna and a rule are rearranged

explanation.surface: Raw fish, under a rule that varies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable' rearranges TUNA A RULE; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Au naturel describes food served plainly, raw or uncooked.

clue.text: When through with it, start yelling in bitterness

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left
per means through or by

indicators.note: start picks the opening letter of yelling

explanation.surface: Once you have finished with it, you begin shouting in resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is harshness or sharpness of manner, akin to bitterness.

clue.text: Promotions are evident as terms develop

indicators.note: develop means change and grow, so the letters of evident as terms are reshaped

explanation.surface: Upgrades become evident as contract terms evolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop' rearranges EVIDENT AS TERMS; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertisements are promotions of products or services.

clue.text: Shows English wine in French church on Sunday

parts.note: vin is the French word for wine
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Englishman serves wine in a French church on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in French' tells you to translate wine. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or reveal a feeling or quality.

clue.text: Soldiers fired one into raised target

indicators.note: into means the first pieces go inside the turned word
raised in a down clue means the word for target is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an aim is a target
lit means set on fire
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Troops shoot one soldier into a target held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AIM to MIA, and 'into' puts LIT and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a body of citizen soldiers.

clue.text: House puts pressure on judge — and a bishop

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a ref, referee, judges a game
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A homeowner leans on a judge and a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated house, assembled from factory-made sections.

clue.text: Copy material and mostly claim original

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric, a material

indicators.note: original read as inventive means the remaining letters are arranged anew
mostly means take most of claim, dropping its final letter

explanation.surface: A fake made of fabric and claiming to be the original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts CLAIM to CLAI, and 'original' rearranges that to LICA. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction, a copy.

clue.text: One in public relations has a harness-trained horse

indicators.note: in means the first piece sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: an ace is one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A PR person owns a trotting horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is a horse trained for harness racing with a lateral gait.

clue.text: Board with no colour, dry and ultimately safe

parts.note: pale means lacking colour
TT is teetotal, i.e. dry

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of safe

explanation.surface: A plain, dry board that is safe in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is the thin board an artist mixes paint on.

clue.text: Kings perhaps confront people with wit

parts.note: to face is to confront
cards are witty, amusing people

explanation.surface: Monarchs come face to face with jokers.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings, queens and jacks are court cards, the pictured ones in a pack; perhaps marks kings as an example.

clue.text: What star signs might reveal about feet?

indicators.note: might reveal suggests the letters lie inside the words star signs

explanation.surface: An astrology question about what the zodiac says about one's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsi are the bones of the ankle and upper foot, so stand for the feet.

clue.text: Sort of view prison sentence — and sigh loudly

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, from bird-lime, rhyming slang for time

indicators.note: loudly means the word sigh is heard, said like letter S then eye

parts.note: sigh is said exactly like S followed by eye

explanation.surface: A prisoner views his sentence and sighs aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD for a prison term is British slang (doing bird). Sigh spoken sounds like 'S-eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's-eye view is one seen from high above.

clue.text: Proof that the Tate perhaps has no right

indicators.note: has no means the abbreviation for right is removed

parts.note: the Tate in London is an art gallery

explanation.surface: Evidence that the Tate lacks justification.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain. A galley is a printer's proof.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley, or galley proof, is a printer's trial copy for checking.
